viva-cpm.description:
Cellular Potts (CompuCell3D-style) backend + processes for the blueprint's
CPM paradigm.

vivarium-tyssue.description:
Vertex / tissue-mechanics processes (tyssue wrapper): DifferentialAdhesion,
DirectionalLineTension, EulerSolver, and the solver/regulation steps.

viva-munk.description:
Center-based 2D physics (pymunk wrapper): PymunkProcess rigid-body dynamics
behind the blueprint's center-based paradigm (MunkBackend).

viva-grammar.description:
The Macklin/PhysiCell cell-behavior hypothesis grammar (Hill-function
signals->behaviors) as a pluggable rule engine. Contributes
BlueprintGrammarProcess, a drop-in alternative to the built-in RulesProcess
for grammar-shaped blueprints (same fates/scalar/divisions/deaths ports;
per_step rate convention). build_core auto-chains viva_grammar.core.build_core.

viva-tellurium.description:
Tellurium / libroadrunner SBML-Antimony ODE bridge. Backs the blueprint's
subcellular "tellurium" module (one RoadRunner ODE solver per cell).

investigations.name: influenza-crossparadigm
investigations.title: Blueprint to pipeline to three substrates: one backend-neutral blueprint, run faithfully on CPM, vertex and center-based, with a pluggable subcellular layer
investigations.description:
This investigation covers the `viva-multicell-blueprint` pipeline end to end: the
backend-neutral blueprint (a versioned, statically validated artifact), the single
`blueprint_pipeline` composite that compiles it onto a mechanics backend, the three
real backends running the full model (reaction-diffusion fields, rules, a systemic
immune ODE fed live by cell counts, latent-pool immune recruitment, per-cell
subcellular ODEs), the comparison layer (`viva_multicell_blueprint.compare`: identity,
raster, metrics) and the interactive figures (`viva_multicell_blueprint.viz`).

**One composite.** `viva_multicell_blueprint.composites.pipeline.blueprint_pipeline`
(a `@composite_generator`, parameterized by `backend` and `blueprint`) is the baseline
composite for every study and drives the Composite Explorer. The earlier
`sego_crossparadigm` composite is a thin alias that delegates to it.

**Five studies.**
  1. blueprint-pipeline-fidelity -- the blueprint contract and t0 fidelity on every backend.
  2. cross-paradigm-equivalence -- fate and position equivalence across the three
     substrates, with the same-backend null and a mechanics-dominated positive control.
  3. substrate-behavior-at-scale -- distance-to-CPM behavior metrics on the large
     Sego tissue, and how the vertex mechanics were matched to the CPM.
  4. dose-response-crossparadigm -- all three substrates agree on the sign of the
     dose response.
  5. subcellular-layer-grow-divide -- the pluggable per-cell ODE layer grows and
     divides cells on all three backends.

**Three substrates, not two.** The center-based model (viva-munk: each cell a circular
rigid body, area-matched to the blueprint `size`) is compiled from the SAME canonical
blueprint via `local:MunkBackend`, shown as a third panel in every spatial playback,
and scored pairwise (cpm-vertex, cpm-munk, vertex-munk). It is deliberately NOT
calibrated to the other two (docs/mechanics.md), so it is a genuinely independent
representation.

**Blueprint contents.** The Sego blueprint pre-places 12 size-25 latent immune cells
(M/NK/CD8_latent) at the tissue margins via `extra_blocks`; recruitment activates that
latent pool in place, and the `infected_seed` is scoped to the main epithelial block so
the latent pool never changes the infected count. All cells are size 25 (size-9 cells
dissolve). Parameters stay faithful to Sego 2022 params.yaml @ b952eec2.

**Reduced scale.** Influenza studies run at a TRACTABLE reduced scale (a 50x50-site
patch, a 6x6 epithelial block) so the runs complete; the large Sego tissue (120x120,
~225-cell epithelium) is used for behavior-metric characterization. This is a
demonstration, not paper scale, and the comparison is reproducible (fixed seeds).

**Anti-goal respected.** No parameter is tuned to force the backends to agree. Honest
divergence is reported.
